source.title: Encapsulation of primary dopaminergic neurons in a GDNF-loaded collagen hydrogel increases their survival, re-innervation and function after intra-striatal transplantation

material: Type 1 bovine collagen hydrogel cross-linked with 4s-StarPEG (1, 2 or 4 mg/ml)

formulation.evidence: For a final volume of 100 µl, 40µl of 5mg/ml type 1 collagen (Vornia Biomaterials), neutralised with 1M NaOH until PH 7 reached, was added to 20 µl of 10x phosphate buffer saline (PBS) containing 4s-StarPEG.
was added to 20 µl of 10x phosphate buffer saline (PBS) containing 4s-StarPEG.
incubated with unseeded collagen hydrogels (2×50 µl gels per well) of various 4s-StarPEG concentrations (1, 2, or 4mg/ml) for 48h or left untreated.

processing.evidence: surface (Teflon®) and placed at 37 °C to gel.

biology.cell_type: E14 ventral mesencephalon primary dopaminergic neurons; GFP bone marrow MSCs

culture_days.evidence: Dopaminergic neuron survival and outgrowth was assessed 48 h after treatment with collagen hydrogels (as described above)

other_outcomes.evidence: the collagen hydrogels successfully formed in situ, were still present 7 days post-infusion (Fig. 3D) and did not result in any striatal damage (not shown).
other_outcomes.name: in vivo hydrogel persistence

notes: Hydrogels incubated with cultures (not seeded); no negative effect on MSC/VM metabolic activity, TH+ survival or outgrowth; values only in figures. In vivo GFP-MSC grafts at days 1, 4, 7 showed similar graft volume.
